  ⎿  Plan saved to: ~/.claude/plans/bubbly-squishing-chipmunk.md · /plan to edit
     Wire nstBuddy frontend to the real backend, rebrand to green, replace meme 
     popup with an academic-integrity disclaimer

     Context

     update-nstBuddy/ (Vite + React 19 + TS + Tailwind v4) and backend/ (Express
     + Prisma/Postgres + Firebase Admin) already exist as separate,
     mostly-built pieces — this isn't a from-scratch build. The backend has real
     routes for campuses, questions, notices, auth, and contributions, and the
     frontend has real pages for campus → semester → question browsing,
     contribution, and Google/Firebase login. The problem is they're wired
     together inconsistently:

     - services/api.ts (the one shared axios client, with auth interceptor)
     points at http://localhost:5001/api, hardcoded.
     - Six other files (CampusSelection.tsx, SemesterSelection.tsx,
     Questions.tsx, ContributePage.tsx, AdminDashboard.tsx, services/auth.ts,
     services/courses.ts) each declare their own const API_URL = 
     'https://update-nstbuddy.onrender.com/api' and call axios directly,
     bypassing the shared client entirely.
     - The frontend .env already defines VITE_API_URL, but nothing reads it —
     every URL is hand-typed per file.

     Net effect: which backend a given page actually talks to depends on which
     file it is, not on any config. That's the opposite of "the website runs on
     this backend." Fixing it means consolidating on one configurable client.

     Two more things ride along with this pass, per your instructions:
     1. Rebrand the accent color from blue to green across the app (confirmed:
     full rebrand, not just a badge).
     2. Replace the meme popup (ExamPopup.tsx, currently shown to everyone on
     every page load) with an academic-integrity disclaimer that requires a
     click-through, is recorded per-user in the database, and re-prompts every 7
     days.

     Out of scope / flagging, not fixing: backend/src/routes/courses.js calls
     prisma.course.findMany(...), but there is no Course model in schema.prisma
     — that route (and services/courses.ts / the /courses nav link, which also
     doesn't have a matching route in App.tsx) is already dead/broken code
     unrelated to the Campus→Semester→Question flow you described. Leaving it
     alone rather than silently expanding scope; flag if you want it removed or
     fixed separately.

     ---
     Part A — Consolidate the frontend onto one configurable backend client

     Backend stays as-is for this part — it already exposes everything the
     frontend needs (/api/campuses, /api/campuses/:slug/semesters,
     /api/questions, /api/questions/filters, /api/questions/contribute,
     /api/contributions/leaderboard, /api/auth/verify-token, /api/notices).

     1. update-nstBuddy/src/services/api.ts: change the hardcoded base URL to
     const API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || 
     'http://localhost:5001/api';
     Add two missing resource groups to this file so every page can import from
     one place:
       - campusesApi: getAll() → GET /campuses, getSemesters(slug) → GET 
     /campuses/:slug/semesters.
       - contributionsApi: getLeaderboard(limit) → GET 
     /contributions/leaderboard.
       - questionsApi: add contribute(data) → POST /questions/contribute (the
     auth-required student endpoint, distinct from the existing admin-only
     create).
     2. services/auth.ts: drop its private API_URL/raw axios, reuse the api
     instance from services/api.ts instead (so it picks up the same base URL,
     interceptor, and credentials config). Add acknowledgeDisclaimer() here
     (Part C).
     3. Pages that currently hardcode the Render URL and call axios directly —
     CampusSelection.tsx, SemesterSelection.tsx, Questions.tsx,
     ContributePage.tsx, AdminDashboard.tsx, UserProfile.tsx (page) — delete
     their local const API_URL = ... and swap the raw axios.get/post calls for
     the corresponding questionsApi / campusesApi / contributionsApi calls from
     services/api.ts. This is a mechanical, per-file swap (same params, same
     response shape — nothing about the request itself changes, just where the
     base URL and auth header come from).
     4. services/courses.ts: leave using its own axios (it's already flagged as
     dead code above) — not worth wiring since the backend route it hits is
     broken.

     Result: exactly one place (VITE_API_URL in .env, already set to the
     deployed Render URL) controls which backend the entire site talks to.
     Pointing local dev at the local backend during testing is just a one-line
     .env change (or an untracked .env.local override), not a code change.

     ---
     Part B — Green rebrand

     No CSS theme tokens exist today (index.css is just @import "tailwindcss" +
     a font rule) — every accent color is a literal Tailwind utility class
     (bg-blue-600, text-blue-600, border-blue-500, ring-blue-500, etc.) repeated
     across ~19 files (CampusSelection.tsx, AdminDashboard.tsx, Footer.tsx,
     ContributePage.tsx, AIUploadPopup.tsx, Questions.tsx, Navbar.tsx,
     UserProfile.tsx (page + component), ExtensionInstall.tsx,
     SemesterSelection.tsx, Login.tsx, Home.tsx, AuthContext.tsx,
     NoticeBoard.tsx, LoadingSpinner.tsx, ProtectedRoute.tsx,
     AssignmentCard.tsx).

     Approach: systematic blue-{shade} → emerald-{shade} replacement across
     update-nstBuddy/src/**/*.tsx (emerald rather than plain green because a few
     emerald accents already exist alongside blue in the current design — e.g.
     the "Active community" dot, "Question Solved" check — so this keeps one
     consistent green family instead of two). This covers buttons, links,
     active-nav underlines, focus rings, spinners, and the Navbar's "2.0"
     badge/notification dot. Gradients that pair blue with purple/indigo (e.g.
     Login page background, Discord banner) get their blue stop swapped to
     emerald too, keeping the second color as-is so they don't turn into a flat
     single-color gradient.

     I'll do this as a targeted find-and-replace pass per file (not a blind
     global sed, since a couple of files use blue- as part of unrelated words) —
     reusing the same class-name swap per file.

     ---
     Part C — Replace the meme popup with an academic-integrity disclaimer

     Current state: components/layout/ExamPopup.tsx shows a meme image + "Brace
     Yourself!" message to every visitor on every load (mounted in App.tsx
     outside the route tree, inside AuthProvider), dismissible via a close
     button, nothing persisted.

     New behavior: a non-dismissable (no close-X — only the acknowledgement
     button) modal shown to logged-in users the first time they arrive, and
     again after any 7-day gap since their last acknowledgement, whose click is
     recorded server-side against their user record.

     Backend

     1. prisma/schema.prisma: add one field to User:
     prisma
     disclaimerAcknowledgedAt DateTime?
     2. prisma migrate dev --name add_disclaimer_ack to generate/apply the
     migration, prisma generate for the client.
     3. routes/auth.js:
       - Include disclaimerAcknowledgedAt in the user object returned by
     /verify-token (so the frontend knows on login/refresh, no extra
     round-trip).
       - New route POST /auth/acknowledge-disclaimer, behind authenticateUser
     (existing middleware in middleware/auth.js), setting
     disclaimerAcknowledgedAt: new Date() on req.user's row and returning the
     updated timestamp.

     Frontend

     1. contexts/AuthContext.tsx: add disclaimerAcknowledgedAt: string | null to
     the User interface; it flows through automatically since user is already
     set from verifyToken's response.
     2. services/auth.ts: add acknowledgeDisclaimer(idToken) → POST 
     /auth/acknowledge-disclaimer with Authorization: Bearer <idToken>.
     3. Replace components/layout/ExamPopup.tsx with
     components/layout/DisclaimerNotice.tsx:
       - Reads user from useAuth(). Computes shouldShow = user && 
     (!user.disclaimerAcknowledgedAt || Date.now() - new 
     Date(user.disclaimerAcknowledgedAt).getTime() > 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).
       - Renders nothing if !shouldShow (covers logged-out visitors on /login,
     and already-acknowledged-this-week users).
       - Modal has no dismiss/close button — only an "I Understand — Continue"
     button. Clicking it calls auth.currentUser.getIdToken() →
     authAPI.acknowledgeDisclaimer(token) → on success, calls refreshUser()
     (already exists on AuthContext) to pull the fresh disclaimerAcknowledgedAt,
     which hides the modal.
       - Disclaimer copy (expanded from your draft, editable after review):
     ▎ Before You Continue
     ▎ This platform is a study reference, not a source of graded-assignment 
     solutions. Using AI/LLM tools, or the linked material here, to directly 
     complete assignments meant to be done yourself may violate your 
     institution's academic integrity policy.
     ▎ We strongly recommend you do not use these links to solve graded work — 
     use them only to cross-check your own understanding after attempting the 
     problem in class. Solutions and concepts taught in class remain the primary
     and intended source of learning.
     ▎ By clicking below, you confirm you understand this and will use nstBuddy 
     responsibly.
     ▎ [ I Understand — Continue ]
     4. App.tsx: swap <ExamPopup /> for <DisclaimerNotice /> (same mount point,
     inside AuthProvider, above the route tree).

     ---
     Verification

     1. Backend: cd backend && npm run dev → confirm GET 
     http://localhost:5001/api/health returns {status: "ok"}; run npx prisma 
     migrate dev and confirm it applies cleanly.
     2. Frontend: point VITE_API_URL at the local backend for this test run, cd 
     update-nstBuddy && npm run dev, open the app in a browser.
     3. Log in with Google → confirm the disclaimer modal appears (no close-X),
     click "I Understand", confirm it disappears and doesn't reappear on
     refresh/nav.
     4. Manually set that user's disclaimerAcknowledgedAt 8 days back (via
     prisma studio or a query) → reload → confirm the modal reappears.
     5. Walk the golden path: Campus selection → Semester selection → Questions
     (search + subject filter, click a question's external link) → Contribute a
     question → see it appear in Questions and the leaderboard update. Confirm
     all of this hits the local backend (check the Network tab / backend console
     logs), not the Render URL.
     6. Visually confirm the green rebrand across Home/CampusSelection, Navbar,
     Login, Questions, Contribute — no leftover blue accents, no broken
     gradients.
     7. Restore VITE_API_URL to the deployed Render URL (or leave the local
     override in an untracked .env.local if you'd rather keep .env pointed at
     prod by default) before shipping.

⏺ Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically — Claude
  checks each tool call for risky actions and prompt injection before 
  executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed, while 
  actions Claude identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a 
  different approach. Ideal for long-running tasks. Sessions are 
  slightly more expensive. Claude can make mistakes that allow harmful 
  commands to run, it's recommended to only use in isolated 
  environments. Shift+Tab to change mode.

⏺ Everything's implemented and verified. Summary:

  Part A — Backend wiring. services/api.ts now reads VITE_API_URL (env-driven)
  instead of a hardcoded URL, and gained campusesApi / contributionsApi /
  questionsApi.contribute. All six pages that were hitting the Render URL
  directly via raw axios (CampusSelection, SemesterSelection, Questions,
  ContributePage, AdminDashboard, UserProfile) now go through that one shared
  client, so the entire site's backend is controlled by one env var. Along the
  way I fixed a real bug in ContributePage's duplicate-question check — it was
  sending campusSlug as the query key when the backend expects campus, so it was
  silently checking across all campuses instead of just the selected one.

  Part B — Green rebrand. Every blue-{shade} Tailwind class across 17 files
  (buttons, nav, focus rings, spinners, badges, gradients) is now
  emerald-{shade}. Confirmed zero blue- classes remain.

  Part C — Disclaimer. Added disclaimerAcknowledgedAt to the User model, a new
  POST /auth/acknowledge-disclaimer route, and the /verify-token response now
  returns it. New DisclaimerNotice.tsx replaces the meme popup — shows only to
  logged-in users, no dismiss button except "I Understand," and re-shows
  automatically 7+ days after the last acknowledgement. I tested the write path
  and the 7-day logic directly against the database with a disposable test user
  (created, verified, deleted — no data left behind).

  One important thing that happened during this: prisma migrate dev tried to
  reset the entire live database (811 real users, 1197 real questions) because
  this repo's migration history was already out of sync with the actual DB. I
  stopped it before it touched anything and used prisma db push instead, which
  applied the new column safely with zero data loss. Worth knowing: that
  migration-history drift is pre-existing and will bite anyone who runs migrate 
  dev here again — happy to fix it properly (rebaseline the migrations) if you
  want, separately from this task.

⏺ Good news: I reproduced the exact CORS check with curl using Origin: 
  http://localhost:5173 and it passes fine (200/204, correct headers, reaches
  the route). So the backend's allowlist itself is correct — but your browser is
  sending a different origin than exactly http://localhost:5173. The most
  common cause: opening the app via http://127.0.0.1:5173 instead of
  http://localhost:5173 — CORS treats those as different origins even though
  they're the same machine.

⏺ Community now has real search and cross-user visibility built in:

  - Search bar at the top of the feed with a Posts/People toggle — Posts mode
  live-filters the feed by content; People mode searches users who've actually
  posted, and clicking one filters the feed to just their posts.
  - Click into anyone — clicking a post's author name/avatar filters the feed to
  that person's posts, same as picking them from People search.
  - Sort toggle — Newest / Most Liked, backed by a real _count-ordered query.
  - Copy Link — every post (not just your own) now has a share option in its
  "..." menu that copies a real permalink (/community?post=<id>); opening that
  link fetches the post directly and scrolls to it with a highlight, even if
  it's not on the first page of the feed.
  - Filter chips (hashtag / author / search) show what's active and can be
  cleared individually or all at once.

  Everything is wired to real backend routes (?search=, ?author=, ?sort=,
  /people/search, /posts/:id) — verified against the live database, no mock
  data.

⏺ Image uploads are live in Community. Summary:

  Security note: you pasted your ImageKit private key in plain chat — I stored
  it only in backend/.env, which is gitignored, and it never reaches the
  frontend. The public key/URL endpoint are exposed to the browser only via a
  short-lived signed token from a new authenticated backend route, which is the
  standard safe pattern. I used your newer key pair (created today, Aug 12 2026)
  — let me know if you'd rather I switch to the May 2025 one.

  What's new:
  - Post up to 5 images per post (composer and edit mode both), any format the
  OS file picker allows — including HEIC from iPhones. Images upload directly to
  ImageKit (never through our server) with a live per-image progress spinner.
  - Display uses ImageKit's f-auto transform, which auto-converts
  HEIC/whatever-you-uploaded into a browser-safe format (JPEG/WebP) on the fly —
  so HEIC photos actually render instead of showing broken images.
  - Posts can now be image-only (no text required) or text-only or both,
  matching Twitter-style behavior.
  - Twitter-style image grid layouts (1–5 images get different layouts) with a
  full-screen lightbox (click to open, arrow keys/buttons to navigate, Esc to
  close).
  - Backend validates: max 5 images, and only accepts URLs actually hosted on
  your ImageKit endpoint (prevents the field being abused to store arbitrary
  URLs).

  Verified end-to-end: real ImageKit signature generation, and a disposable DB
  test confirming the images array round-trips through Postgres correctly. Build
  is clean, both dev servers healthy.

  Groups (new, from scratch)
  - Create a group with a name, description, category, and a hard member cap
  (2–100).
  - Browse/search all groups, or view "My Groups" (created + joined), with live
  progress bars and Full/Closed badges.
  - Joining requires sharing a contact method (WhatsApp, phone, or email) —
  verified this is not visible to other members, only to the group admin and to
  you (confirmed with a disposable DB test: member1 could see their own contact
  but not the admin's).
  - As admin: edit the group, close it to new joins without deleting it, remove
  any non-admin member, or delete the group outright.
  - As a member: leave anytime (admins delete the group instead, so it's never
  orphaned).
  - Verified capacity enforcement and duplicate-join protection directly against
  the database before wiring up the UI.

  overlapping avatar header, a compact sticky sidebar (stats as a list, not five
  duplicate icon-boxes), and a tabbed content area (Contributions / Posts /

⏺ All four fixes are shipped and verified:

  1. Admin master control — new "Users" and "Community" tabs in Admin Dashboard:
  - Users tab: every registered user, their role/activity, and a Ban from 
  posting toggle (server-enforced — banned users get a 403 on creating posts or
  comments, verified with a direct DB test).
  - Community tab: every post site-wide, rendered with the same PostCard used
  elsewhere, so admin gets real Edit/Delete on any post (not just their own) —
  verified the permission logic against author, admin, and random-user cases.
  - Safety rail: admins can't ban themselves, and can't ban other admins.

  2. "Edited" tag — was already there but easy to miss on posts (plain gray

  pill badge next to the timestamp.

  card and as the hero background on the group detail page; groups without one
  keep the existing gradient-icon fallback so nothing looks broken.

  ## Brand & Style                                                              
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The design system embodies a **Technocratic Elite** personality—ambitious,    
  high-performance, and future-forward. It positions educational excellence     
  through the lens of "Deep Tech" and "AI Leadership," targeting high-achieving 
  students and industry-focused stakeholders.                                   
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The visual style is a blend of **Corporate Modern** and **High-Contrast       
  Bold**. It utilizes a dark-mode-first aesthetic for emotional impact in       
  tech-heavy sections, contrasted with high-utility light surfaces for dense    
  information like curriculum details. The aesthetic is punctuated by           
  "AI-centric" visual cues: subtle grid-line backgrounds, data-visualization    
  graphics, and precision-engineered layouts that evoke the feel of a high-tech 
  lab or a modern fintech platform.                                             
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Colors                                                                     
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The palette is rooted in a high-contrast relationship between **Deep Tech     
  Blue** and neutral surfaces.                                                  
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Primary Blue**: Used for critical CTAs ("Apply Now"), branding, and key   
  interactive states.                                                           
  - **Secondary Gold**: Reserved for achievement-oriented callouts, prestige    
  indicators (e.g., "Go for Gold"), and high-level metrics.                     
  - **Neutral/Backgrounds**: The system uses `#16191D` for immersive, "Deep     
  Tech" dark sections and `#FFFFFF` for information-dense curriculum areas.     
  `#F6F7F9` serves as a subtle background for secondary cards to maintain       
  hierarchy without adding visual noise.                                        
  - **Urgency/Alerts**: A vibrant red-orange is used sparingly for              
  time-sensitive elements like "Applications closing" countdowns and "NEW"      
  tags.                                                                         
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Typography                                                                 
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The typography system prioritizes extreme hierarchy to manage the density of  
  university data. **Hanken Grotesk** (a high-precision substitute for Mona     
  Sans) provides a technical, wide-set feel for headlines and metrics, while    
  **Inter** ensures maximum legibility for curriculum descriptions and body     
  copy.                                                                         
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Metrics**: Large numbers (placements, stipends) should always use the     
  `metric-xl` style to create immediate visual anchors.                         
  - **Headlines**: Use heavy weights (700-800) for section titles to maintain   
  the authoritative tone.                                                       
  - **Labels**: Small, uppercase labels with increased letter spacing are used  
  for tags like "NEW" or "BATCH OF 2024."                                       
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Layout & Spacing                                                           
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The system follows a **12-column fixed grid** on desktop, transitioning to a  
  fluid single-stack on mobile.                                                 
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Modular Rhythms**: Use a base unit of 8px. Card internal padding is       
  typically 24px or 32px to ensure a "breathable" high-end feel.                
  - **Vertical Storytelling**: Section gaps are intentionally generous (120px+) 
  to separate different phases of the student journey (Curriculum vs.           
  Placement).                                                                   
  - **Data Grids**: Use consistent 24px gutters for grids containing student    
  cards or faculty profiles to maintain structured alignment.                   
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Elevation & Depth                                                          
                                                                                
                                                                                
  Visual hierarchy is established through **Tonal Layering** and                
  **Glassmorphism**:                                                            
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Layered Surfaces**: Dark sections use surface-on-surface colors (e.g.,    
  `#16191D` background with slightly lighter `#22262B` cards) to create subtle  
  depth without shadows.                                                        
  - **AI-Centric Glows**: High-priority modules (like "Deep Tech" features)     
  utilize subtle blue backdrop blurs and semi-transparent glass layers to       
  emphasize the futuristic theme.                                               
  - **Precision Outlines**: Use low-opacity white or blue borders (1px) for     
  cards on dark backgrounds instead of heavy shadows to maintain a "blueprint"  
  or "schematic" technical feel.                                                
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Shapes                                                                     
                                                                                
                                                                                
  The shape language balances approachability with technical precision.         
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Standard Containers**: All cards, curriculum boxes, and informational     
  modules use a **Rounded (8px)** corner radius.                                
  - **Interactive Elements**: Primary CTAs ("Apply Now") use **Pill-shaped**    
  (full radius) borders to differentiate actions from static content.           
  - **Status Tags**: Status indicators (e.g., "Accepted," "Published") use      
  pill-shaped containers with a 4px horizontal padding to resemble mechanical   
  labels.                                                                       
                                                                                
                                                                                
  ## Components                                                                 
                                                                                
                                                                                
  - **Primary Buttons**: Pill-shaped, high-contrast blue backgrounds with white 
  `label-sm` text. Use a subtle glow effect on hover for the "AI-centric"       
  feel.                                                                         
  - **Secondary Buttons**: Outlined blue or white with pill-shaped corners.     
  - **Data Cards**: White or light-grey backgrounds with 1px borders. These     
  should contain a clear `metric-xl` value, a `headline-md` title, and brief    
  `body-md` copy.                                                               
  - **Timeline Indicators**: Vertical 2px lines with numbered circles (01-06)   
  to guide users through the admission process. Use the primary blue for active 
  steps.                                                                        
  - **Status Chips**: Small, high-contrast badges (e.g., "NEW" in status-urgent 
  red) placed in the top-right corner of cards or news items.                   
  - **Navigation Tabs**: Campus-wise selection tabs use an underline indicator  
  in the primary blue to show the active state.

⏺ Everything's clean and verified.

⏺ Everything's shipped. Summary:

  1. Color theme rebrand
  - Site-wide swap from the emerald green accent to the Technocratic Elite blue
  (#0057c1 primary) via a proper Tailwind v4 @theme color scale (brand-50 →
  brand-900) — mechanically replaced across all 38 files that used the old
  accent, so hover/focus/badge states all stay consistent.
  - Headings now render in Hanken Grotesk, body text in Inter (both loaded via
  Google Fonts).
  - Dark CTA sections switched from the old dark-green to the spec's #16191D
  Deep Tech dark.

  2. College / Others contribution flow
  - Fixed a real bug in the process: the old "custom course" path silently set
  semester: "0", which the backend's own validation (semester must be 1–8) would
  have rejected — it never actually worked.
  - Schema now properly supports it: semester/campusId are optional, plus a new
  customCourse field. Verified both flows end-to-end against the live database.
  - ContributePage has a real College/Others pill switch; Others mode shows just
  a course-name field (with autocomplete from existing course names), no
  semester.
  - Home page now has a matching Campuses/Other Courses toggle; picking a course
  jumps straight to its questions — no semester screen, via a new /course/:name
  route.
  - Redesigned SemesterSelection from the "big number tile" grid into a
  numbered-timeline list, matching the spec's Timeline Indicator component.

  3. Home page now shows a "Recently in Community" rail alongside "Recently
  Added" questions, pulling real posts from the Community feed.

  4. Footer + watermark — real multi-column footer (Product/Account links,
  including a genuine new Privacy Policy page so nothing is a dead link) with a
  large translucent "NSTBUDDY" wordmark, plus a "Built by Narendra Singh"
  credit. Added a styled console banner and an HTML comment credit that survives
  the production build (verified in dist/index.html).

  Both dev servers are live and healthy, and I also found and killed a stale
  orphaned backend process from earlier in the session that had been silently
  serving old code.

⏺ Everything's shipped and verified:

  Custom courses now support image + description
  - Admin's "Add Course" form (in Admin Dashboard → Courses) now has a banner
  image uploader (reusing the ImageKit pipeline) and a description field.
  - These show on the homepage's "Other Courses" cards — image as a top banner
  with the name overlaid (matching the campus card style), description as a
  preview line. Courses without an image fall back cleanly to the icon-block
  style.
  - Fixed a related gap: courses used to only appear once someone contributed a
  question to them; now they show up on the homepage the moment an admin creates
  them, real image and description included.

  Semester Selection redesigned again, this time more substantially:
  - Full hero section matching the rest of the site (grid-texture background,
  animated count-up stats: total questions, active semesters, most-active
  semester).
  - Semester cards are now real cards with a subtle giant watermark numeral
  (same technique as the footer wordmark), a progress bar, an "Active" badge,
  and staggered entrance + hover-lift animation — a genuine step up from the
  previous timeline-list version.

  Subject field is now an autocomplete, not free text — while testing I
  confirmed the exact problem you were describing already exists in the data
  (multiple near-duplicate variants of "Gen AI", a "DSA " with a trailing space,
  etc.). The Subject field on the Contribute page now suggests existing
  subjects via a live-loaded list, while still letting a student type a
  genuinely new one if needed.

  Build is clean, backend restarted, all changes verified against the real
  database.

  working).
  - Site admins can now also delete any group, even ones they didn't create and
  aren't a member of — surfaced as a "Site admin" delete control on the group
  detail page, kept separate from the normal join/leave/creator flow so an admin
  can still join a group as a regular member too if they want.
  - Enforced server-side (not just hidden in the UI) — verified with a direct
  test that a random non-admin, non-creator user is still rejected.

  Verified against the real database including an actual delete-with-cascade,
  and confirmed the API now returns a canModerate flag consistent with the
  pattern already used for Community post moderation.
